title: Automation lanes for track, group and return parameters
description:
## Why
While writing the demo `examples/brass-floor.apr`, the build-up needed the brass to start raw and have EQ and then compression arrive over bars 1–5. With no automation, each stage became a copy of the track over its own bars: nine brass tracks instead of three. Filter sweeps, fade-ins and "the reverb opens up in the breakdown" are impossible. Automation is a breakpoint lane per parameter, the same idea as a DAW's automation lanes. That form is readable text for a human, a structure an agent can edit, and a lane a future UI editor can draw.

## The feature in one example
```apr
track stab  voicing triad  steps ". . . x _ _ x _ _ _ . . . x _ _"  filter lp 20000
  eq    highcut 20k  low +2@200
  comp  3:1  -22dB  attack 15ms  release 150ms  mix 0%
  send  plate 10%
  automate eq.highcut   1=20k  3=6k  5=5k        # the old-record hiss rolls off over bars 1-4
  automate comp.mix     step  1=0%  5=100%        # compression arrives exactly at the drop
  automate send plate   1=10%  12=10%  13=40%     # the reverb opens in bar 12
  automate filter       1=300  5=20k              # a low-pass sweep over the build
  automate volume       1=-60dB  2=0dB            # fade in over bar 1
  automate pan          1=-30  5=30
```

## Language (.apr)
A new **indented line** `automate <target> [step] <point> <point> …` is allowed under a `track`, `group` or `return`. **Not under `master` in this task**: a master `automate` line is an error, "`automate` on the master isn't supported yet; automate a group track that everything plays through". The master chain runs live on the audio thread, and that is a separate task.

**Point:** `<position>=<value>`. Position is a bar or `bar:beat`, 1-based, exactly as `at` positions (reuse `parse_position`, score.rs:1032). The value is written in the parameter's own units, as on the effect line (`6k`, `-4dB`, `30%`, a bare pan number).

**Curve:**
- Before the first point, the lane holds the first value. After the last point, it holds the last value.
- Between points it ramps linearly in the parameter's natural scale:
  - frequencies: in log frequency (octaves), so a sweep sounds even;
  - dB values: linear in dB;
  - shares (%): linear;
  - pan: linear.
- `step` (right after the target) holds each value until the next point instead of ramping.
- Two points at the **same position** make an instant jump in either mode (`12=10% 13=10% 13=40%`).
- Positions must not go backwards. A position past the end of the piece is an error.

**Targets (v1):**

| Target | Where | Units / range | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `volume` | track, group, return | dB, −60…+12 (≤ −60 dB means silence) | Added to the track's or bus's static `volume` (the fader). It is an offset lane, so `automate volume 1=-60dB 2=0dB` is a fade-in to the fader level. |
| `pan` | track | −100…100 | Replaces the static `pan` for the whole piece. |
| `send <return>` | track | % or dB, as on the `send` line | Replaces that send's level. The track must already have `send <return> …` on a send line. |
| `filter` | track | Hz, 20–20000 | The cutoff of the track's `filter lp|hp`. The track must have a `filter` option, which gives the type and is the value when there's no automation. When automated, the filter runs at stem level (see Engine), not per note. |
| `eq.lowcut`, `eq.highcut` | track, group, return | Hz, 20–20000 | That band must be on the eq line. |
| `eq.low`, `eq.high` | track, group, return | dB, ±24 | The shelf's gain. The frequency stays as written on the eq line, and the shelf must exist on the eq line. |
| `comp.threshold` | track, group, return | dB, −60…0 | |
| `comp.mix` | track, group, return | %, 0–100 | **New `mix` parameter on `comp`** (parallel compression): `comp 3:1 -22dB mix 50%`. Default 100%. Add it to the comp line itself too, not only automation. |
| `reverb.mix`, `delay.mix` | track, group, return | %, 0–100 | The existing wet share. |
| `width` | track, group, return | %, as on the width line | |

- `eq.highcut` means the **first** eq in the chain; `eq2.highcut` means the second eq, `comp2.mix` the second comp, and so on.
- A target naming an effect the chain doesn't have is an error.
- The same target automated twice on one track or bus is an error.

**Errors** point at the `automate` line, not the track header. The `SourceMap` (dsl.rs:32) currently points all track errors at the header; add what's needed so automation errors carry the automate line and a column. Use the house style (`suggest()`, exact fragments):
- `line 9 column 12: unknown automation target \`eq.hicut\` (did you mean \`eq.highcut\`?)`
- `… automate eq.highcut: this track's eq has no highcut; add one to the eq line (eq highcut 20k)`
- `… automate comp.mix: this track has no comp`
- `… automate send plate: this track doesn't send to \`plate\`; add send plate 0% to automate it`
- `… automate filter: this track has no filter; add filter lp 20000 (or hp) to the track line`
- `… automate eq.highcut: point 3: position 2 comes before 5; points go in time order`
- `… automate volume: position 25 is past the end of the piece (bar 20)`
- `… automate eq.highcut: 50k is outside 20Hz to 20000Hz` (reuse the ranges in `check_effects`, compile.rs:35)
- `… automate eq.highcut is already automated on this track`
- `… \`automate\` on the master isn't supported yet; automate a group track that everything plays through`

## YAML
Mirror the existing YAML mix conventions in docs/yaml.md "## Mixing" (numbers in the same units the YAML already uses for that parameter). Add to tracks, groups and returns:
```yaml
automate:
  - target: eq.highcut
    points: [["1", 20000], ["3", 6000], ["5", 5000]]
  - target: comp.mix
    step: true
    points: [["1", 0.0], ["5", 1.0]]
```
Positions are strings ("3", "3:2"). `deny_unknown_fields` as elsewhere. Also add `mix` on `comp`. `.apr` → YAML → `.apr` must round-trip (the examples test does this for every example).

## Score model and format
- `TrackSpec`, `GroupSpec` and `ReturnSpec` get `automate: Vec<AutomationSpec>`.
- `AutomationSpec { target: String, step: bool, points: Vec<(String position, f64 value)> }`, or an equivalent you design. Keep the value in the same unit the YAML uses.
- `CompSpec` gets `mix: Option<f64>`.
- `format()` prints automate lines after `send` lines, one per lane, with values in their natural units (`20k`, `-4dB`, `30%`), so that `parse(format(s)) == s`.
- `dsl::effect_text` prints `mix N%` on comp when set.

## Compile / Timeline
- `TrackInfo` and `BusInfo` get `automation: Vec<Lane>`, skipped in JSON when empty.
- `Lane { target: String, step: bool, points: Vec<[f64; 2]> }`, where points are `[beat, value]` in engine units:
  - Hz for frequencies;
  - dB for gains, volume and threshold;
  - 0–1 for shares (mix, send);
  - −1…1 for pan;
  - width as the engine takes it.
- The target is canonical: `eq.highcut`, `eq2.highcut`, `send.plate`, `filter`, `volume`, `pan`, `comp.mix`, …
- All validation from the Language section happens at compile time (or parse time where it's purely syntactic), with the errors above.
- When `filter` is automated, events of that track must **not** carry the per-note `filter` (the stem-level filter replaces it). Otherwise the per-note filter is unchanged, and so is the cache.
- `Timeline::explain_mix()` (compile.rs:1717) lists each lane under its track or bus: `automate eq.highcut 1=20k 3=6k 5=5k`.

## Engine
All automation for tracks, groups and returns is applied **offline in `Renderer::arrange`** (render.rs:86) and `Mix::build` (mix.rs:85), so it reaches the CLI render, `play` and web playback automatically. A curve is evaluated at score time: the loop position `i % n`, mapped to beats, **plus the `--bars` start offset `b0`** (render.rs:121). Loop wrap must be continuous: `process_chain` tiles cycles, so evaluate at `i % n`.

Build one small shared module, e.g. `crates/apricity-engine/src/automation.rs`: `Curve::from_lane(&Lane, sr, spb, offset_beats, loop_frames)` with `value_at(frame) -> f64`. Unit-test it on its own for linear, log-frequency, step, jump and hold-before/after.

**Control rate:**
- Gain, pan, send and mix/width values are interpolated **per sample**.
- Filter and EQ coefficients and the compressor threshold are recomputed every **32 samples** with `Biquad::set` / `Eq::set` / `Compressor::set`. These keep filter memory (fx.rs:37, 118, 193), so there's no zipper noise and no reset clicks.

**Where each target applies:**
- `filter`: a stem-level `Biquad` (12 dB/oct, same response as `render.rs::biquad`, render.rs:296) run over the summed track stem **before** its insert effects.
- `eq.*`, `comp.*`, `width`: inside `master::process_chain` (master.rs:266). The `rt` arm (330-340) currently runs a fixed `MasterChain`. When the chain has automation for that effect, process in 32-sample blocks and `set()` the new params before each block. Keep the fixed path untouched when there's no automation (byte-identical output for existing scores).
- `comp.mix`: dry/wet around the compressor, per sample, like reverb/delay's `mix()` (master.rs:279-297).
- `reverb.mix` and `delay.mix`: replace the constant `m` with the curve value per sample.
- `volume` (track): a per-sample gain curve applied to the stem **after** insert effects, before pan and sends (fader position).
- `volume` (bus): the same, applied after the bus's effects, in place of or multiplied with the constant `b.gain` (mix.rs:134).
- `pan` (track):
  - For a track going to a bus, apply per-sample `balance(pan)` in `Mix::build` (mix.rs:116) instead of the constant.
  - For a track going straight to the master, bake the per-sample balance into the stem buffer and set `Stem.pan = 0`, so the live mixer (arrangement.rs:89) applies no extra pan. Check that `balance(0)` is unity.
- `send <return>`: a per-sample level curve at mix.rs:122.

**Web:** in `web/src/audio/player.ts` (around 235-260), a track that has automation must go **whole** to one worker, like a track with effects, because comp automation is nonlinear. That is the only web change; don't touch `web/src/ui/*` or styles.

Existing scores without `automate` must render **bit-identically** (the fixed-parameter paths stay as they are).

## Docs
- `docs/language.md`:
  - a new "### Automation" subsection under "## Mixing", with the example above, the targets table, curve rules and `step`;
  - add `automate` to "Where each line goes";
  - add `mix` to the comp row of the Effects table;
  - add the new errors to "Mistakes and messages";
  - Grammar: `track-line = effect | "pan" … | "send" … | automate`, with `automate = "automate" TARGET [ "step" ] POINT { POINT }`, `POINT = POSITION "=" VALUE`, and allow automate under group/return.
- `docs/yaml.md`: the `automate` field under Mixing, plus comp `mix`.
- Write for musicians; match the existing tone.

## Tests (all must be real assertions on real code)
- **dsl.rs unit tests:**
  - parse every target;
  - `step` and jumps;
  - format round-trip;
  - every error message above, asserting "line N" and the exact fragment.
- **tests/compile.rs:**
  - lanes reach the Timeline with the right beats and engine units (e.g. `3=6k` becomes `[8.0, 6000.0]` in 4/4; `30%` becomes 0.3; pan `-30` becomes -0.3);
  - per-note filter is removed when `filter` is automated;
  - YAML round-trip.
- **Engine tests:**
  - `Curve` unit tests.
  - A `volume 1=-60dB 2=0dB` lane on a constant tone: RMS of the first 10% of bar 1 is at least 40 dB below bar 2.
  - `eq.highcut 1=20k 3=1k` on white noise: energy above 5 kHz in bar 3 is at least 15 dB below bar 1.
  - `comp.mix step 1=0% 2=100%`: bar 1 equals the dry input (within 1e-6), and bar 2 differs.
  - A step jump lands on the exact frame of the bar line.
  - `--bars 3-4` rendering starts the curve at bar 3's value.
  - A score with no automation renders bit-identically to before: compare against a render made before your change, or assert the fixed path is taken.
- `cargo test -p apricity-score -p apricity-engine -p apricity-dsp` passes, and so does the examples round-trip test.

## Out of scope
- Master automation.
- Automating reverb decay or delay time/feedback (those processors have no setters).
- Per-note filter curves.
- Any UI.
- A separate task will add per-note `attack`/`release` envelopes (don't add them here).

## Done means
Everything above is implemented, tests pass under the watchdog, docs are updated, and there are no dependency changes. The reviewer re-runs the tests, renders a demo with automation, and listens.
